Authors / PI: Lynda Olman; Benjamin J. Hatchett; Meghan Collins; Anne Heggli; Kathryn Lambrecht; Zach Tolby; Dominic Charles
Brief Abstract: Abstract. A case study in methods reveals a way that false responses to online surveys can be leveraged to add rhetorical value to technical communication research. Serendipitously, we discovered during our study of community commonplaces of weather-forecast discussions that open-ended bot responses contained phrases very close to rhetorical commonplaces generated by humans. Using freely available text-mining tools, technical communication researchers can easily mine false responses for indicators of community beliefs, norms, and values.
